title: Salt in a beaker: the thermometer
hook: Stir 80 g of a salt into 500 g of water at 20 °C. Where does the thermometer go?

knows: that fires and many reactions give out heat
doesNotKnow: that some processes absorb heat from their surroundings
that dissolving a solid can cool the water

misconception: Chemical changes always release heat, and a cold pack stores cold.
objective: The learner can say that dissolving 1.0 mol (80 g) of ammonium nitrate takes about 25.7 kJ from 500 g of water, cooling it by about 11 °C, because the process absorbs heat from its surroundings.

claims.text: Dissolving ammonium nitrate in water absorbs about 25.7 kJ of heat per mole (an enthalpy of solution of about +25.7 kJ/mol).
claims.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, enthalpy of solution of NH4NO3 about +25.7 kJ/mol at 25 °C (infinite dilution).

claims.text: One mole of ammonium nitrate weighs about 80 g, so 80 g is 1.0 mol and one scoop of 20 g is 0.25 mol.
claims.source: NH4NO3 molar mass 14.01×2 + 1.008×4 + 16.00×3 = 80.04 g/mol (IUPAC atomic weights).

claims.text: Warming 1 g of water by 1 °C takes about 4.18 J; the mixture is treated the same way.
claims.source: Specific heat of liquid water about 4.18 J/(g·K) at 25 °C (CRC Handbook). Treating the salt solution as 4.18 J/(g·K) is an approximation (real solutions are a little lower, so the real drop is slightly larger).

claims.text: Dissolving 1.0 mol (80 g) in 500 g of water takes about 25.7 kJ from the water and cools it by about 11 °C, from 20 °C to about 9 °C.
claims.source: 25,700 J / ((500 + 80) g × 4.18 J/(g·K)) = 10.60 K; 20 − 10.6 = 9.4 °C (node; Demo.tsx drop(n)). Scoops: 0.25 mol each, temperature drop = heat absorbed over (total mass × 4.18).

claims.text: Heat flows from the water into the dissolving salt, so the water cools; this is how an instant cold pack works.
claims.source: Instant cold packs contain ammonium nitrate or urea and water in separate compartments (Chemistry LibreTexts, Enthalpy of solution; Atkins, Physical Chemistry). Endothermic dissolution: positive enthalpy of solution.

claims.text: Model: an insulated beaker with no heat from the room, and the salt dissolves completely.
claims.source: Stage label 'insulated'. Ammonium nitrate solubility about 190 g per 100 g water at 20 °C, so 80 g in 500 g dissolves fully (CRC Handbook).

recall.question: A student dissolves a salt in water and the thermometer falls. The dissolving process…
options: made no heat change at all
recall.why: A falling temperature means heat left the water and went into the dissolving salt, so the process absorbed heat.
